headline: A significant storm Wednesday into Thanksgiving brings widespread rain (an inch or less around Charlotte, 1–2 inches along the Blue Ridge Escarpment) and frequent 30–40 mph gusts that can topple tents and holiday decorations, with stronger mountain-ridge gusts of 50 mph or more under a Wind Advisory.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Tonight clouds thicken from south to north around Charlotte and the Piedmont, with gusty northeast winds as strong high pressure builds down the East Coast. Temperatures fall into the mid to upper 30s across most of the Piedmont, and a few spots near I-40 and in mountain valleys near the Blue Ridge Escarpment could drop below freezing.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Rain chances spread from south to north on Wednesday, mostly spotty and light during the day around Charlotte before steadier rain arrives in the evening; a brief trace of sleet, snow or freezing rain is possible early Wednesday where it's still near freezing, but only bridges and overpasses would likely get slick. In the Piedmont, frequent 30–35 mph gusts (peaking near 40 mph) are expected from Wednesday afternoon through Thursday morning, strong enough to blow over holiday decorations, tents and canopies and possibly cause isolated power outages; secure outdoor cooking appliances and keep a fire extinguisher handy. Rain continues Wednesday night and tapers from southwest to northeast on Thanksgiving, totaling an inch or less in much of the Piedmont and 1–2 inches along the Blue Ridge Escarpment, with a low flood risk (a Marginal, level 1 of 4, risk of excessive rain). In the mountains, a Wind Advisory runs from noon Wednesday to 10 AM Thursday for Avery County and elevations above 3,500 feet in Buncombe, northern Jackson and the counties bordering Tennessee, where ridgetop gusts of 50 mph or more could cause power outages; after a lull and near-normal temperatures Thursday afternoon, gusty winds return Thursday night through Friday, with a slight chance of light snow, wintry mix or rime ice near the Tennessee border Thursday night through Friday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Temperatures trend warmer over the weekend. A fast-moving disturbance could bring a small chance of rain around Sunday, with only rain expected since the wetter scenarios are also the warmer ones.

watch_for: Wind gusts of 30–40 mph in the Piedmont and 50+ mph on mountain ridges Wednesday afternoon through Thursday morning; the Wind Advisory could expand to lower elevations.
A trace of freezing rain, sleet or snow early Wednesday could make bridges and overpasses slick on a busy travel day.
A narrow band of heavier rain west of the storm's track could locally raise rain totals.
confidence: Forecasters are highly confident in the Wednesday–Thursday storm and its gusty winds, less certain about the storm's exact track and rain totals, and the weekend outlook carries only small rain chances.
